pairs: Yet truly, Agrippa said to Paul,
“It is permitted for you to speak for yourself.”
Tunc Paulus extenta manu cœpit rationem reddere:
Then Paul, extending his hand, began to offer his defense.
De omnibus quibus accusor a Judæis,
“I consider myself blessed, O king Agrippa,
rex Agrippa, æstimo me beatum apud te cum sim defensurus me hodie,
that I am to give my defense today before you, about everything of which I am accused by the Jews,
especially since you know everything that pertains to the Jews,
et quæ apud Judæos sunt consuetudines
propter quod obsecro patienter me audias.
I beg you to listen to me patiently.
Et quidem vitam meam a juventute,
quæ ab initio fuit in gente mea in Jerosolymis,
all the Jews know about my life from my youth,
which had its beginning among my own people in Jerusalem.
præscientes me ab initio (si velint testimonium perhibere) quoniam secundum certissimam sectam nostræ religionis vixi pharisæus.
They knew me well from the beginning, (if they would be willing to offer testimony) for I lived according to the most determined sect of our religion: as a Pharisee.
in spe quæ ad patres nostros repromissionis facta est a Deo, sto judicio subjectus:
it is in the hope of the Promise which was made by God to our fathers that I stand subject to judgment.
in quam duodecim tribus nostræ nocte ac die deservientes,
It is the Promise that our twelve tribes, worshiping night and day,
hope to see. About this hope,
De qua spe accusor a Judæis, rex.
O king, I am accused by the Jews.
Quid incredibile judicatur apud vos, si Deus mortuos suscitat?
Why should it be judged so unbelievable with you all that God might raise the dead?
Et ego quidem existimaveram me adversus nomen Jesu Nazareni debere multa contraria agere,
And certainly, I myself formerly considered that I ought to act in many ways which are contrary to the name of Jesus the Nazarene.
This is also how I acted at Jerusalem.
et multos sanctorum ego in carceribus inclusi,
I enclosed many holy persons in prison,
having received authority from the leaders of the priests.
And when they were to be killed,
Et per omnes synagogas frequenter puniens eos,
And in every synagogue, frequently while punishing them,
And being all the more maddened against them,
I persecuted them, even to foreign cities.
In quibus dum irem Damascum cum potestate et permissu principum sacerdotum,
Thereafter, as I was going to Damascus, with authority and permission from the high priest,
de cælo supra splendorem solis circumfulsisse me lumen,
I and those who were also with me,
et eos qui mecum simul erant.
saw along the way a light from heaven shining around me with a splendor greater than that of the sun.
Omnesque nos cum decidissemus in terram,
And when we had all fallen down to the ground,
audivi vocem loquentem mihi hebraica lingua:
I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew language:
durum est tibi contra stimulum calcitrare.
It is hard for you to kick against the goad.’
For I appeared to you for this reason:
so that I may establish you as a minister
and a witness concerning the things that you have seen,
and concerning the things that I will show to you:
eripiens te de populo et gentibus,
in quas nunc ego mitto te,
and the nations to which I am now sending you,
in order to open their eyes,
ut convertantur a tenebris ad lucem,
so that they may be converted from darkness to light,
et de potestate Satanæ ad Deum,
and from the power of Satan to God,
so that they may receive the remission of sins
and a place among the saints,
per fidem quæ est in me.
through the faith that is in me.’
I was not unbelieving to the heavenly vision.
sed his qui sunt Damasci primum,
first to those who are at Damascus
and then to the entire region of Judea,
doing the works that are worthy of repentance.
It was for this reason that the Jews,
having apprehended me when I was in the temple,
Auxilio autem adjutus Dei usque in hodiernum diem,
But having been aided by the help of God, even to this day,
I stand witnessing to the small and the great,
nihil extra dicens quam ea quæ prophetæ locuti sunt futura esse, et Moyses,
saying nothing beyond what the Prophets and Moses have said would be in the future:
and that he would be the first from the resurrection of the dead,
lumen annuntiaturus est populo et gentibus.
and that he would bring light to the people and to the nations.”
While he was speaking these things
Festus said with a loud voice:
multæ te litteræ ad insaniam convertunt.
Too much studying has turned you to insanity.”
but rather I am speaking words of truth
sed veritatis et sobrietatis verba loquor.
For the king knows about these things.
latere enim eum nihil horum arbitror.
For I think that none of these things are unknown to him.
Neque enim in angulo quidquam horum gestum est.
And neither were these things done in a corner.
In modico suades me christianum fieri.
“To some extent, you persuade me to become a Christian.”
et in modico et in magno,
sed etiam omnes qui audiunt hodie fieri tales,
but also all those who hear me this day will become just as I also am,
and those who were sitting with them.
“This man has done nothing worthy of death,
aut vinculis dignum quid fecit homo iste.
if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
